description: Textual rules that locate places where TLS certificate verification is weakened or redirected to a custom trust anchor. A textual match is evidence about configuration, never about an actual interception; the status is reported as 'known_indicator' for unambiguous verification-disabling switches and 'suspicious' for patterns that are frequently, but not always, a real bypass.

rules.title: Git certificate verification disabled in a config file
rules.description: http.sslVerify=false makes git accept any server certificate, which defeats the entire purpose of patching the CA store.
remediation: Remove the sslVerify setting and re-run `git config --get http.sslVerify` to confirm it is unset.
If a corporate TLS-inspecting proxy was the reason, configure http.sslCAInfo with the proxy's CA instead of disabling verification.

rules.title: GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY enabled
rules.description: GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY disables certificate verification for every git transfer in that environment, including CI clones.
remediation: Delete the variable from the script, Dockerfile or CI definition.
Re-run the failing clone and fix the underlying trust problem instead.

rules.title: npm strict-ssl disabled
rules.description: strict-ssl=false lets the package manager install from a registry presenting any certificate.
remediation: Remove strict-ssl=false from .npmrc (project, user and global scopes).
Point `cafile` at the proxy CA if a TLS-inspecting proxy is in use.

rules.title: NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0
rules.description: Node.js disables all TLS certificate verification for the process when this variable is 0.
remediation: Remove the variable.
Use NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS with a specific CA file when an extra trust anchor is genuinely required.

rules.title: rejectUnauthorized: false in source
rules.description: A TLS client or agent created with rejectUnauthorized:false accepts forged certificates for the hosts it contacts.
remediation: Remove the option, or scope it to a test fixture that only talks to a local server.
Supply a `ca:` option with the specific certificate when connecting to an internal host.

rules.title: verify=False passed to an HTTP client
rules.description: requests/httpx calls with verify=False skip certificate validation. The match is textual: confirm the call is an HTTP request and not an unrelated keyword argument.
remediation: Remove verify=False, or replace it with verify='/path/to/internal-ca.pem'.
For a deliberate test against a local server, keep it but isolate it in test code.

rules.title: Unverified SSL context created
rules.description: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables hostname and chain verification; assigning it to _create_default_https_context does so process-wide.
remediation: Delete the assignment and pass an explicit `cafile`/`capath` where a private CA is needed.

rules.title: PYTHONHTTPSVERIFY=0
rules.description: Disables HTTPS certificate verification for the whole Python process.
remediation: Remove the variable from the environment, script or CI definition.

rules.title: curl invoked with --insecure / -k
rules.description: curl -k accepts any certificate. Frequently found in install scripts and Dockerfiles, where it also defeats supply-chain integrity.
remediation: Drop the flag and let curl use the updated CA bundle.
If the host uses a private CA, pass --cacert with that CA file.

rules.title: wget --no-check-certificate
rules.description: Downloads proceed regardless of the certificate presented.
remediation: Remove the flag; use --ca-certificate for a private CA.

rules.title: Go tls.Config InsecureSkipVerify: true
rules.description: The Go TLS client performs no chain or hostname verification.
remediation: Remove the field, or set RootCAs to a pool containing only the expected internal CA.

rules.title: reqwest danger_accept_invalid_certs(true)
rules.description: The builder is explicitly told to accept invalid certificates.
remediation: Remove the call; use add_root_certificate() for a private CA.

rules.title: Java trust-all manager or permissive hostname verifier
rules.description: Common names for X509TrustManager implementations that accept any chain. Confirm the implementation actually skips validation.
remediation: Replace with the platform default trust manager and import the needed CA into the JDK truststore or a dedicated keystore.

rules.title: .NET ServerCertificateValidationCallback overridden
rules.description: An overridden validation callback may legitimately pin a certificate or may blanket-return true. Read the callback body before judging.
remediation: Ensure the callback returns false for any SslPolicyErrors it does not explicitly expect.

rules.title: pip trusted-host configured
rules.description: pip skips TLS verification for a trusted-host index, so packages from it are installed without certificate checks.
remediation: Remove trusted-host and configure `cert = /path/to/ca.pem` for the internal index instead.

rules.title: Composer disable-tls enabled
rules.description: Composer downloads packages over plaintext or without verification.
remediation: Set disable-tls to false and fix the underlying certificate problem.

rules.title: Package repository referenced over http://
rules.description: A plaintext repository URL needs no forged certificate at all to be tampered with.
remediation: Switch the repository URL to https://.

rules.title: TLS error silently swallowed
rules.description: Swallowing a TLS error can hide exactly the certificate rejection that indicates a blocked compromised CA, or hide a successful interception.
remediation: Log and re-raise the error instead of passing.

rules.title: Custom CA bundle override configured
rules.description: An override means the process does NOT use the OS trust store, so patching the OS does not necessarily fix this project. The referenced bundle must be checked for the compromised SPKIs separately. Only the variable name and the file it was set in are reported; the value is never printed.
remediation: Scan the referenced bundle: `ca-trust-audit project --scan-bundle <path>`.
Rebuild or replace the bundle from an updated upstream source if it still contains a compromised SPKI.

sources.used_for: the requirement that certificate verification must not be disabled to work around a certificate error
the categories of weakened TLS configuration worth looking for in a project
